source.title: SAEBER: Sparse Autoencoders for Biological Entity Risk

record.file_problem: The full post is present. Some mathematical notation in the SAE equations is missing or unrendered, but the rest is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Extends SAE feature analysis to protein folding and design models and reports feature-level virulence associations; it does not test the original toy-network geometry or LLMs.
record.gate_note: Only V4 is tested: the post reports virulence-associated SAE features in protein models. The logistic-regression classifier AUROCs, including the raw-versus-SAE comparison, measure classification performance rather than whether representations are superposed, so they are not rows. The post does not report feature overlap geometry, capacity competition, or feature stability/completeness.
record.test_reason: The post uses SAEs as a tool for virulence probing in protein models and reports classifier and feature-association performance. It never tests whether features are superposed, spread across neurons, or recovered as sparse features in an LLM. V4 is about real (LLM) models, and AUROC for a virulence label does not show superposition or sparse-feature recovery. The post's only polysemanticity remark is an untested hypothesis.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that raw and SAE activations support virulence classification, with a best AUROC of about 0.82 to 0.88 (below DTVF at 0.92). They also say SAE features give interpretable, feature-level virulence attributions. The claim that block 12 SAE 'untangles polysemantic features' is a hypothesis only.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Matryoshka BatchTopK SAEs and virulence-feature scoring in protein models, rather than the original toy-network experiments on superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature AUROC increases with layer depth, especially for RFDiffusion3.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual SAE features in RFD3/RF3 reach up to ~0.8 AUROC for virulent versus benign designs, and the AUROC rises with layer depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features in protein design and folding models can carry class-specific signal such as virulence.

record.problems: The authors report a small dataset (275 sequences; 220 training and 55 test designs), limited compute, and layer selection based on LLM SAE literature rather than systematic ablation. Feature AUROC uncertainty and model- and layer-specific values for the reported maximum are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Classifier AUROCs and the raw-versus-SAE comparison in Results were left out because they measure virulence classification performance, not the representational properties named by the claim.

untested.parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity transitions.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
Features spread across neurons and sparse feature recovery were not measured, and the setting is protein models, not LLMs.
SAE feature completeness, stability, canonical status.

record.verdict_notes: This is a 48-hour hackathon post with n=275 and no per-feature uncertainty. The reader's V4 'supports' label should be dropped. The record's own gate note says the post does not test superposition.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
The post does not test whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The post does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE feature associations in protein folding and design models, not LLMs; does not measure features spread across neurons or establish that the associated features are semantically complete.
Does not test SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
Does not test whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: RFDiffusion3 and RoseTTAFold3 SAEs (aggregate; model-specific attribution of the maximum not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Scored individual SAE features against virulent/benign labels using univariate AUROC.

conditions.value: SAE features across tested layers; model-specific maximum not stated

rows.measure: Feature AUROC for association with virulent designs
rows.value: Certain features score above chance, up to ~0.8 AUROC
rows.locator: Results, paragraph beginning 'Certain features fire above chance'
rows.note: Aggregate statement; the post does not identify which model or layer produced the maximum. Virulence association provides limited evidence of detectable SAE features, not a test of complete or canonical feature recovery.
rows.check: Univariate AUROC against a virulence label measures class association, not whether features spread across neurons or whether a dictionary recovers sparse features. The row is in a protein model, not an LLM. The maximum is not attributed to a model or layer, and no baseline is given.

conditions.value: tested layers; individual values not stated

rows.check: The depth trend in feature AUROC for virulence is a measure of label association, not superposition or sparse-feature recovery. No per-layer values are given. The rows should not link to V4.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE features in the tested protein folding and design models
reader_labels.reason: Some SAE features show above-chance virulence association, with reported AUROC up to ~0.8 (r1); feature AUROC also increases with depth, especially in RFDiffusion3 (r2). This is evidence in protein models, not LLMs, and does not establish semantic completeness.
